title: Customs Amendment (Immediate Destruction of Illicit Tobacco) Bill 2019
short_title: Customs Amendment (Immediate Destruction of Illicit Tobacco) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would allow customs officials to destroy seized illicit tobacco products immediately instead of storing them for 30 days.
The Comptroller-General of Customs would be given the power to decide how to handle tobacco products seized as prohibited imports from 1 July 2019, including immediate destruction.
The bill is part of the government's 2018-19 Budget measure to tighten tobacco border controls, and similar destruction powers already exist for other prohibited imports like psychoactive substances.
changes: Empowers the Comptroller-General of Customs to cause seized tobacco products to be dealt with as they see fit, including immediate destruction.
Removes the current requirement to store seized prohibited imports for a minimum of 30 days before disposal.
Aligns tobacco products with existing controls for other prohibited imports such as psychoactive substances.
summary.affected: Australian Border Force officials and tobacco importers are affected by the bill.
